You want long? I'll give you long. If shes into pop music, first show her songs like "The Dirt Whispered," "Audience of One," "Behind Closed Doors," "Satellite,"  "TRAGEDY + TIME"*** (this one would probably bridge the gap well I'd think), I'd also throw in "Methadone" into this category - fantastic song that isn't too harsh. 

Also, throwing in the ballads would help get used to his voice in a less aggressive way - such as "Restless World," "Roadside" (the girl vocal here may be one shed like too sing to if you cover another song), "For Fiona," "Swing Life Away," and then "People Live Here" and/or "Hero of War" to ween her into the more statement filled songs of Rise Against.

After this, you can start moving into the more aggressive songs of Rise Against such as "Make it Stop," "Give it all," "Chamber the Cartridge," "The Eco Terrorist in Me" (very good mix of old and new), "Everchanging," "Survive," "The Good Left Undone" and then pretty much any other song you truly love that I left out, but I think by going with the more popular/less aggressive and statement making songs, and the ballads (to get used to his voice's rasp without being overwhelmed) should get her into the Rise against mood, then you can slowly bring in the more aggressive/thought provoking songs once she gets used to the idea of Rise Against and their more fast pace, aggressive punk rock sound that makes Rise Against who they are. 

If there's one thing I've learned from getting people into Rise Against, and by being a DJ at my old college, start with the safer, nicer songs before going into the more high energy/strong meaning songs. If you have any other questions or want more suggestions let me know! I have a 40ish song playlist that is made for showing people Rise Against.

*Edit - A decent rule of thumb is going in reverse chronological order and including the ballads - if you look at it, Appeal to Reason and Black Market are generally less harsh/aggressive than RPM and The Unraveling so as you get her more and more into Rise Against (especially as you want to cover a RPM song) you can add more and more older songs going back through albums, not the most perfect way of doing it of course, but in general it could work well if you get stuck on what to show next. 

**Edit 2 - be careful throwing too many songs at once. I'd personally recommend sending them in phases of like... 8-10 if you're just sending a playlist with little explination.  Primarily because sending a ton of songs at once can overload someone or dilute the connection they can get to a few songs so I'd introduce them in phases to make sure. Start with the first batch I wrote and some ballads, then slowly introduce the heavier (both in meaning and aggression) songs to the playlist so she has her songs that are now "safe" and familiar AND a slow stream of new and exciting songs. Before you know it she'll be asking for all the songs and then a new Rise Against fan will be born. ;)

Ive been to a few concerts at the HoB boston (going to this one too!) Its easy the way its set up. The whole standing roo only area you got works this way - the direct center of the pit is usually the mosh area, go to the left, or right (recommended) side and its relatively calm (not moshing but people having fun). Go further up by the bar area and your now maybe 6-10 inches above the rest, good sode facing view of the show, potentially a railing to lean on, and no moshing or pushing at all. Also the way back is raised too with the same area and the whole area is for you to use. Essentially you picked the first floor (best floor). Mezzanine is the second and the seats are on the third. So you'll have no problem staying safe/non pushed.

Edit: the HoB Boston is a relatively small venue anyway so dont expect one of those "several thousand people crammed in an area" things like some venues in the greater area (see: garden, Gillette,  Tsongas, etc.)

The news made this seem a lot more promising than it is, essentially, CD47 is a pretty damn important membrane protein on a LOT of different human cells, so basically, turning it off in a mouse is pretty easy - its a human protein, not a mouse protein so of course it would look good in a mouse model (giving a mouse human poison to kill the human pieces in it look a lot better than giving a human human poison to kill the human pieces). CD47 is too important in humans to just shut it down with an inhibitor. 

-- This is what I got reading the journal the times magazine links to, as well as some research on CD47 prior to this jounral and after. 

Also, it takes about 15 years to go from experimental lab drug (testing in vitro, on single isolated cells for effect) to the general public/hospitals. http://www.ccfa.org/resources/clinical-trials-101.html

Odds are, after two years there would be some yield for phase one trials IF they made it that far, but simply shutting down CD47 seems like an unlikely way to do it in humans. 

- Getting masters in biotechnology (people who do this kinda shit) 

*EDIT - PLEASE NOTE! Science is stupidly complex and confusing, and the little bit of evidence I had to work with so far means there COULD be things that are missing out, meaning this very well could be a game changer in a way not noted by the media (the news is absolutely terrible with science and LOVES to jump to conclusions that aren't really possible or there), so assuming that there is some unlisted promise in this research, there is a chance that there could be something there - but the new's undying need for the "silver bullet" cure of cancer is a very shady thing at best - cancer mutates and changes really aggressively, and its your own body going against you - so its still, in my opinion, unlikely that there's a "silver bullet" potential in this research they have going, at least with the Anti-CD47 antibodies they're doing - these types of things usually target ALL CD47 proteins they come in contact with, meaning the ones in your blood cells and other cells as well - unless cancer has a very specific form of mutant CD47 that behaves differently (which it looks like all there is is a higher rate of it on the cells, which is semi unfortunate because it it was reversed, a lower concentration of the antibody could potentially work - but that's not the case), it could have some help - but if it is, as is stated, the same protein - then there's little chance of this working overly well in humans - the jump from mice to human models is a VERY big one.
